text_blocks.snippet: A first mortgage is the primary loan used to purchase a property, giving the lender a first claim (lien) on the property in case of default. It's the initial loan taken out to buy a home, and it typically has priority over any other subsequent mortgages or liens on the same property.

list.title: Secured by the Property:
list.snippet: A first mortgage is secured by the property itself. If the borrower fails to make payments, the lender can foreclose on the property and sell it to recover the outstanding loan amount.

list.title: Priority in Repayment:
list.snippet: In the event of a foreclosure, the first mortgage lender is paid back first from the sale proceeds. Any subsequent liens or mortgages on the property are paid only after the first mortgage is settled.
